title: perf: compute cue time-remaining once per cue in sort comparators
author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #135.

Both active-cue sorts in `app/app/index.tsx` — `onAirActiveBlocks` (fullscreen/OnAir path) and `activeBlocks` (normal home view) — recomputed each cue's time-remaining *inside* the sort comparator. Because `Array.prototype.sort` calls its comparator ~`n·log n` times, the time-zone conversion (`computeCountdown` → `Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts`) ran far more often than needed on every 1-second tick, in both of the app's most time-critical render paths.

Switched both to the standard decorate-sort-undecorate: `map` each cue to `{ block, total }` (computing `computeCountdown(...).total` once per cue), `sort` on the precomputed `total`, then `map` back to blocks. The redundant `.slice()` is dropped because `.map()` already returns a new array. Same contents, same ascending order, same output shape.

### Watch out for
- Sort order/output must stay byte-identical — both sorts are pure numeric ascending (`a.total - b.total`) using the exact same inputs as before, so this is a mechanical equivalence with no behavioral change.
- No new abstraction was introduced: each call site is fixed in place rather than sharing a helper, per the issue's scope note and CLAUDE.md's minimalism rule.
- Lint in this environment reports pre-existing module-resolution errors (`@expo/vector-icons`, `expo-keep-awake`) across many files unrelated to this change; the edit adds no new lint issues and touches no imports.

title: Sort comparators in index.tsx recompute computeCountdown O(n log n) times instead of O(n)
author: claude[bot]
body:
**What to optimise:** Every 1-second tick, the app re-sorts the active cues list by time-remaining so the soonest cue shows first. The sort currently recomputes each cue's remaining time *inside the comparator function* instead of once beforehand. Because `Array.prototype.sort` calls its comparator roughly `n·log(n)` times (not `n` times), this means the relatively expensive time-zone conversion (`computeCountdown`, which calls `Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts`) runs far more often than needed — once per comparison instead of once per cue.

**Where:**
- `app/app/index.tsx:2095-2101` — `onAirActiveBlocks` sort (fullscreen/OnAir path), `totalFor` called twice per comparison.
- `app/app/index.tsx:2142-2150` — `activeBlocks` sort (normal home view), same pattern via `totalFor`.

Fix is a standard decorate-sort-undecorate: compute `{ block, total }` once per block into an array, sort that array by the precomputed `total`, then map back to blocks. No change to sort order or output shape.

**Expected gain:** For `n` cues, current cost is `~n·log2(n) × 2` calls to `computeCountdown` per render (each comparison calls `totalFor` on both sides); the fix drops this to exactly `n` calls. For a realistic 5-10 cue list that's roughly 20-65 calls down to 5-10 — a 3-6x cut in `computeCountdown`/`Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts` invocations on every single tick, in both the normal and OnAir (fullscreen, "viewed from a distance") render paths. This is textbook sort-comparator-recomputation waste, not a guess — the call count math follows directly from how `Array.sort` invokes its comparator.

**CLAUDE.md priorities served:** the 1-second ticker is named explicitly as a hot path in this project's scan criteria (\"a wasted allocation or an avoidable re-render there costs real battery and real smoothness\"). This reduces redundant work in that exact hot path, on both the primary home view and the full-screen OnAir view that CLAUDE.md says must be the most visible, fastest-updating part of the app.

**STEP 4 scope check:** One file (`app/app/index.tsx`), two small, adjacent, mechanical edits (each under ~10 lines, well under the ~100-line/one-file budget). No architecture, state shape, or component structure changes — `activeBlocks`/`onAirActiveBlocks` keep the exact same contents and order. Does not touch any listed invariant (stateless passed-cue derivation, beep pool, Notifee channels, ABI/packaging settings, backend/accounts/sync rules all untouched).

**How to verify on the Xiaomi Mi A2 Lite:** with `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEBUG_LOGS=1`, add a temporary counter/log around `computeCountdown` (or wrap it in the debug log) to count calls per render with, say, 8 active cues configured; confirm the count drops from roughly 8·log2(8)×2 ≈ 48 to 8 per tick after the fix. Separately, use React DevTools/Perf or a simple `performance.now()` wrapper around the sort block to confirm reduced time-in-render per tick, and visually confirm the cue ordering and timer display are unchanged in both the home view and full-screen OnAir view.

## Also spotted
`app/lib/time.ts:128-132` — `computeCountdown`'s `get()` helper does a linear `.find()` over the `formatToParts` array three separate times (hour/minute/second) per call; could be flattened to one pass. Smaller in scope than the sort issue above (a handful of lines saved per call vs. eliminating whole extra calls), so left unfiled this run.

title: Un-nest the TimeStepper remount key's template literal in CueEditModal
author: yanukadeneth99
body:
What's worth improving and why:
In the CueEditModal component, the `key` prop passed to `TimeStepper` is built from a template literal that has a second template literal nested inside one of its `${...}` slots. Nested template literals are harder to scan at a glance than a plain variable reference, and the fix is a pure refactor with zero behavior change, which makes it a safe, low-risk cleanup.

Where it is:
`app/components/CueEditModal.tsx:493`

```tsx
key={`${existing ? `edit-${existing.id}` : "add"}-${autoOpenSection ?? "none"}`}
```

Sonar rule and message:
Rule `typescript:S4624`, quoted message: "Refactor this code to not use nested template literals."

Suggested fix:
Sonar's guidance for this rule is to pull the inner template literal out into its own named variable so the outer template literal only interpolates plain values, removing the nesting. Applied here:

```tsx
const timeStepperKey = `${existing ? `edit-${existing.id}` : "add"}-${autoOpenSection ?? "none"}`;
```

becomes two steps immediately above the `TimeStepper` JSX:

```tsx
const idPart = existing ? `edit-${existing.id}` : "add";
const timeStepperKey = `${idPart}-${autoOpenSection ?? "none"}`;
```

and then use `key={timeStepperKey}` on the `TimeStepper` element instead of the inline expression.

Smallest safe way to make the change:
This is a two-line extraction right before the `TimeStepper` element (around line 485-493) with no change to the resulting string value, so the remount-key behavior described in the surrounding comment (forcing `TimeStepper` to remount when switching between Add/Edit modes or between target fields) is completely preserved. No other files or call sites reference this expression.

CLAUDE.md invariant to respect while fixing:
The existing comment directly above the `key` prop (lines 486-492) explains *why* the remount key is shaped this way - keep that comment intact (or move it to sit above the new variable) so the reasoning isn't lost, per the project's comment guidelines (comments must stay short, simple, and explain non-obvious WHY). Do not change the actual key string produced, since this key is load-bearing for TimeStepper's autoOpen behavior described in the Architecture section of CLAUDE.md.

author: claude[bot]
body:
CI lint failure isn't fixable with a mechanical patch — this bump needs to wait on upstream.

**Root cause:** `website/` uses `eslint-config-next@16.2.10`, which pulls in `eslint-plugin-react@^7.37.0` as a transitive dependency. That plugin's react-version detection code calls the legacy `context.getFilename()` API, which ESLint 10 removed. Every lint run crashes immediately with `TypeError: contextOrFilename.getFilename is not a function`.

**Why this can't be patched locally:** I checked the latest available versions — `eslint-config-next@16.2.12` (current stable) still depends on `eslint-plugin-react@^7.37.0`, and `eslint-plugin-react`'s newest release (`7.37.5`) still declares `peerDependencies.eslint: "^3 || ... || ^9.7"` — no ESLint 10 support exists yet anywhere in this dependency chain. title: Cache zone1 midnight timestamp instead of recomputing it with Luxon every tick
author: claude[bot]
body:
What to optimise: Every single second, the app recalculates "what time is midnight today in the primary timezone" from scratch using the Luxon date library, even though that answer only changes once every 24 hours. It throws away the work and redoes it 86,400 times a day for a value that is correct almost the whole time. The fix is to remember (cache) the last computed midnight timestamp and only redo the calculation when the calendar day in the primary zone actually changes.

Where: app/app/index.tsx:468, inside the passedAt derivation (useMemo at app/app/index.tsx:466-481):

    const z1MidnightMs = DateTime.fromJSDate(now).setZone(zone1).startOf("day").toMillis();

This line runs on every 1-second tick (useNow), for as long as the app is open, regardless of how many cues exist.

Expected gain: This Luxon call (which builds at least two DateTime objects, resolves the zone1 timezone offset, and does calendar truncation) runs roughly 86,400 times per day, but its result is identical for about 86,399 of those calls -- it only changes at the zone1 day boundary or when zone1 itself is changed in settings. Caching it (keyed on the zone1 calendar date) cuts that to effectively 1-2 recomputations per day, removing over 99.99% of the redundant work from the once-a-second tick path. Luxon operations are consistently measured as several times slower than native Date/Intl calls in JS benchmarks, so on a low-end chip like the one in the Xiaomi Mi A2 Lite this is real, if small, per-tick CPU/battery savings -- and it is savings taken directly off the same 1Hz tick that also drives the countdown render and the final-3-second-beep scheduler, so any headroom clawed back there keeps the time-critical work on schedule.

CLAUDE.md priorities served: battery/CPU efficiency and "stay minimal and fast" for the always-on 1-second ticker; indirectly supports timing accuracy by reducing per-tick JS main-thread work in the same loop that schedules the sync-critical countdown and beep.

Scope check (Step 4):
- 1 file (app/app/index.tsx), roughly 15-20 lines added/changed, all localized inside the existing passedAt useMemo (plus one new useRef declared alongside the other refs at the top of the component).
- No architecture change: no state moves, no new component, no new files.
- No invariant touched: the derivation stays fully stateless with respect to now -- the cache key is itself derived fresh from now/zone1 every tick, so if the ticker is suspended (background, device sleep) and resumes on a different day, the date-key mismatch forces an immediate recompute. This preserves the documented "no edge detection, no TTL, re-derive every tick" design (app/app/index.tsx:444-455) -- this only skips redundant Luxon math when the derived key has not changed, it does not skip the derivation itself. Does not touch alarms, the beep pool, Notifee channels, ABIs, or packaging settings.

How to verify on the Xiaomi Mi A2 Lite: With a JS profiler attached (Flipper / Chrome remote debugger performance tab) while the app sits idle with a handful of cues configured, record self-time of the passedAt useMemo callback over about 60 seconds before and after the change. Expect the per-tick self-time attributable to the Luxon midnight computation to drop to near-zero on all but the first tick and the tick that crosses midnight. Also confirm functionally: change the device clock across a zone1 midnight (or wait for it) and verify passed cues still un-minimize together exactly as before.

Also spotted (not filed): passedAt (index.tsx:466-481), the final-beep primary lookup (index.tsx:582-589), and the active-cue sort (index.tsx:2145-2154) each independently call computeCountdown per cue per tick -- up to 3x redundant Intl-based countdown computations per cue per second. body:
Closes #138.

## What changed and why

On Android, **Settings → Reset All** cleared cues from state and storage but never cancelled their scheduled `AlarmManager` triggers. Those triggers survive app restarts and Doze, so a deleted cue would still fire later — in alarm mode a full-screen, lock-screen takeover with looping audio and vibration for a "Target #N" cue that no longer exists, with nothing to dismiss.

The fix mirrors the existing single-cue delete path (`removeBlock`): inside `doReset`, before clearing state, loop over `targetBlocksRef.current` and fire-and-forget `cancelAnyAlert(b.notificationId)` for each block that has one. This covers both entry points (native Alert and web ConfirmModal) since both route through `doReset`.

- `multiRemove` is unchanged (never `AsyncStorage.clear`), so `analyticsEnabled` is still preserved.
- Cancels are fire-and-forget (`.catch(() => {})`), so Reset All stays snappy.
- Reads from `targetBlocksRef.current` (not `targetBlocks`) to avoid the stale-closure risk in the `[]`-deps `useCallback`, matching `removeBlock`.
- `cancelAnyAlert` is already null-safe and a no-op off Android.

Single-file change to `app/app/index.tsx`. `npx expo-doctor` passes 19/19.

### Watch out for
- The issue's "Also spotted" note (`autoMinimizePassed`/`finalBeep` not reset by Reset All) was explicitly out of scope and is **not** included here.
- Cancels are intentionally not awaited before `setTargetBlocks([])`; this is the established fire-and-forget idiom in this file, not an ordering bug.
